title: Operational Compendium: Policies, Procedures, and Templates
author: Priya Narayanan
content:
Overview

Purpose: This compendium collects Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standardized templates for access & permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and common internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees and managers executing routine operational decisions.

Scope: Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with Redwood systems, finances, or data. Exceptions require documented approval from the owning team and Finance or Legal where indicated.

Owner and maintenance: The Finance & Legal team maintains procurement, expenses, and vendor-management sections. People Ops maintains travel and people-facing templates. Security owns access, permissions, and data management sections. Contact: policies@redwood-inference.com.

Policy matrix (high level)
- Access & Permissions: Role-based access by default; principle of least privilege; periodic review cadence. Owner: Security.
- Change Management: Risk-based RFCs and release windows with automated gating for production. Owner: Eng Platform.
- Data Management: Classification, retention, encryption, and deletion standards. Owner: Security & Data Compliance.
- Procurement & Expenses: Approval thresholds, preferred vendors, centralized PO process. Owner: Finance.
- Vendor Management: Risk assessment, contract minimums, periodic review. Owner: Finance & Legal.
- Travel: Pre-approval, per diem, booking guidance, and expense reconciliation. Owner: People Ops.

Section 1 — Access & Permissions
1.1 Principles\- All access requests must be justified with a business reason, TTL (time-to-live) when temporary, and an owner.\- Use "rbac.redwood-inference.com" for role assignments (internal IAM).\- Privileged roles (e.g., infra-admin, db-admin, kms-admin) require manager + security approval.

1.2 Provisioning workflow (standard)
1) Employee/contractor requests access via Access Request Form (template below).
2) Request is routed to the resource owner for approval within 48 hours.
3) Security performs Privilege Review for sensitive scopes (PII, keys, production DB).
4) Provision automated via SCIM/Okta connector where supported. Manual grants logged in the access audit tracker.

1.3 Periodic review\- Quarterly role review for all production-facing roles.
- Annual audit for all users with access to PII or export-controlled data.

1.4 Emergency escalation\- Security on-call must be notified immediately for suspected misuse. Communicate via #security-incident and PagerDuty.

Section 2 — Change Management
2.1 Change classification\- Minor: non-customer-impacting configuration or documentation changes. No RFC required; pre-commit CI and canary deploy recommended.\- Major: code or infra changes that may impact latency, billing, or availability for customers. Requires RFC, rollout plan, and release window.\- Critical: security patches, data-migration fixes, or incidents requiring immediate action; follow incident process and retrospective.

2.2 RFC and release process (major changes)
1) Author prepares RFC in the RFC template (title, summary, risk classification, rollback plan, testing matrix).
2) Stakeholders: Eng Platform, SRE, Product, Security, and Finance (if cost impact). Send RFC for 72-hour review unless expedited.
3) Pre-release checklist: unit/integration tests, perf test (latency & throughput baseline), canary target (min 1% traffic), monitoring dashboards, alert thresholds.\4) Release window: standard weekday 09:00–17:00 PT unless otherwise approved. Emergency releases isolate after-hours approvals policy.

2.3 Post-deploy validation\- 60-minute observation for canary; metrics tracked: error rate (<0.1%), p50/p95 latency within baseline +20%. If threshold exceeded, rollback immediately.

2.4 Change rollback SLOs\- Time-to-rollback target: 30 minutes for high-severity regressions, 4 hours for functional regressions affecting fewer than 5% of customers.

Section 3 — Data Management
3.1 Classification\- Public: safe to publish.\- Internal: accessible by employees.\- Confidential: PII, customer data, model-training datasets, and export-controlled data.

3.2 Retention and deletion\- Hot logs: 90 days.\- Backups (encrypted): 365 days.\- Long-term archives: up to 7 years (subject to legal holds).\- Data deletion requests: follow data subject request (DSR) playbook; acknowledged within 3 business days.

3.3 Storage and encryption\- All Confidential data must be encrypted at rest with KMS keys (customer-managed where requested in Private deployments). TLS 1.2+ for in-transit.

3.4 Access for analytics and dev\- Use anonymized or synthetic datasets when possible. Any request to copy production data for dev/analytics must be approved by Data Compliance and logged with a TTL.

Section 4 — Procurement & Expenses
4.1 Approval thresholds (effective 2026)\- <= $5,000: direct manager approval.\- $5,001–$50,000: Director + Finance approval.\- $50,001–$250,000: VP-level approval + Finance.\- > $250,000: Executive committee (CEO/CFO) + Legal + Finance.

4.2 Purchase order (PO) process\- All vendor spend requires a PO issued through the Procurement portal (procurement.redwood-inference.com) before goods/services begin, except for recurring cloud bills covered under the Cloud Subscription policy.

4.3 Preferred vendors and exceptions\- Finance maintains a preferred-vendor registry (cloud partners, software, professional services). Exceptions require a Vendor Exception Form and procurement committee approval.

4.4 Expense policy highlights\- Employee reimbursements must be submitted within 30 days.\- Non-itemized alcohol is disallowed on expense reports without Executive approval.\- Corporate card policy: cards issued at manager discretion; employees must reconcile monthly.

Section 5 — Vendor Management
5.1 Onboarding minimums\- Contract must include: data protection addendum (DPA), security SOC2 or equivalent evidence where applicable, liability and indemnity clauses, termination & data return instructions.

5.2 Risk assessment matrix (summary)
- Low: SaaS with no sensitive data (quarterly review).\- Medium: SaaS with internal data or vendor personnel access to non-sensitive systems (biannual review).\- High: Any vendor with access to PII, production systems, or model-training data (triannual review + penetration test evidence).

5.3 Offboarding checklist
1) Revoke all credentials and API keys.
2) Confirm data export and secure deletion per contract.
3) Update inventory and notify teams.

Section 6 — Travel & Business Expenses
6.1 Pre-approval and booking\- All overnight travel requires manager approval in Travel Portal. Book via our Travel partners (TravelPortal.redwood-inference.com) to ensure insurance and preferred rates.

6.2 Per diem and reimbursement\- Domestic: $75/day meals; International: follow per-country rates in Appendix A. Receipts required for meals > $25.\- Lodging: book standard rooms; any upgrade requires manager approval and justification.

6.3 Safety and insurance\- All employees traveling for work are covered by company travel insurance. Emergency assistance contact: travel-assist@redwood-inference.com.

Appendix C — Audit & reporting cadence\- Monthly: Finance reports (open POs, recurring spend).\- Quarterly: Vendor risk reviews and access certification.\- Annually: Full policy review and tabletop exercises.
